# ADO Epic Template

Use this template when creating or updating Epics in Azure DevOps via MCP. Epics represent large bodies of work spanning multiple Features — typically a bounded context, major capability, or program initiative.
page_texts.3:
[.claude/templates/ado/epic.md#title]

### Title

Short, outcome-oriented title. Do not prefix with "Epic:" — ADO already knows the work item type.

**Format:** `<Verb> <Business Capability or Outcome>`

**Examples:**

- Modernize Claims Adjudication Processing
- Implement Member Eligibility Verification Service
- Establish Provider Management Module
page_texts.4:
[.claude/templates/ado/epic.md#description]

### Description

Structure the description using this format:

```markdown
## Business Context

Why this Epic exists — the business problem or opportunity it addresses.
Reference the Medicaid program context, CMS requirements, or state mandate where applicable.

## Scope

What bounded context(s) or business capabilities this Epic covers.
List the high-level Features expected under this Epic.

- Feature 1 — brief description
- Feature 2 — brief description
- Feature 3 — brief description

## Out of Scope

Explicitly state what this Epic does NOT cover to prevent scope creep.

## Success Criteria

How we know this Epic is done — business-level outcomes, not technical tasks.

- [ ] <Measurable outcome>
- [ ] <Measurable outcome>

## Dependencies

Other Epics, external systems, or decisions this depends on.

## Compliance and Regulatory

CMS certification requirements, HIPAA considerations, state-specific mandates, or waiver conditions that apply.
```
page_texts.5:
[.claude/templates/ado/epic.md#priority]

### Priority

Map to ADO priority values:

| ADO Priority | Meaning | Maps to BA Priority |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 - Critical | Regulatory or contractual obligation | P0 |
| 2 - High | Core functionality or major business need | P1 |
| 3 - Medium | Important but not blocking | P2 |
| 4 - Low | Nice to have | P3 |
page_texts.6:
[.claude/templates/ado/epic.md#area-path]

### Area Path

Set to the team or domain area that owns this Epic (e.g., `MMES\Claims`, `MMES\Eligibility`, `MMES\Provider`).
page_texts.7:
[.claude/templates/ado/epic.md#iteration-path]

### Iteration Path

Set to the target Program Increment (PI) or release milestone, not a sprint — Epics span multiple sprints.
page_texts.8:
[.claude/templates/ado/epic.md#tags]

### Tags

Apply tags for cross-cutting concerns:

- Bounded context name (e.g., `claims`, `eligibility`, `provider`)
- `hipaa` if PHI is involved
- `cms-certification` if CMS MECT requirements apply
- `state-specific` if driven by a single state's mandate
page_texts.9:
[.claude/templates/ado/epic.md#links]

### Links

- **Related Requirements** — link to `docs/requirements/` files using `AB#<id>` references
- **Architecture Decisions** — link to ADRs in `docs/decisions/` that govern this Epic's design
- **Child Features** — ADO parent/child links to Features under this Epic
page_texts.10:
[.claude/templates/ado/epic.md#guidelines]

## Guidelines

- One Epic per bounded context or major business capability — do not combine unrelated domains
- Write from the business perspective, not technical implementation
- Include CMS/state compliance context when applicable — this is Medicaid work
- Keep the scope section concrete — vague Epics become unmanageable
- Reference glossary terms from `docs/glossary.md` for consistent language
- When creating an Epic, also create a corresponding entry in `docs/project-plan.md` with the `AB#<id>` reference
